description: The literal LENGTH bound (ISO §2023:8.3.3.2.3 SR1 alphanumeric, 8.3.3.4.3 SR1 boolean, 8.3.3.5.3 SR1 national; 8.8.3.2 SR2-SR4 for a concatenation's result): 8,191 character positions from COBOL-2014, 160 below it - a RELAXATION, so a 161-position literal compiles at 2014 and 2023 and is rejected below 2014 with COBOL0814 (also under --permissive: a length error, not a removed construct), the word-length row's posture. A literal longer than 8,191 positions is rejected at EVERY edition. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1 'The implementor must allow for nonnumeric literals of 1 through 160 characters in length.'; §2002:8.3.1.2.1.2 SR1 bounds an alphanumeric literal 'greater than zero and less than or equal to 160 alphanumeric character positions' (§2002:8.3.1.2.3.2 SR1 and §2002:8.3.1.2.4.2 SR1 the boolean and national literal alike, §2002:8.8.3.2 SR2 'the length of the value resulting from concatenation shall be less than or equal to 160 alphanumeric character positions'); §2014:8.3.1.2.1.2 SR1 'shall be less than or equal to 8,191 alphanumeric character positions' (§2014:8.3.1.2.3.2 SR1, §2014:8.3.1.2.4.2 SR1 and §2014:8.8.3.2 SR2 alike), and §2014:E.3 item 15 records the change: 'have been increased from 160 character positions to 8,191 character positions' (VCR row 7.43). ONE bound, CobolLiteral.MaxPositions(edition), read by LiteralScreen (every literal token) and by ConcatFolder.ResultLengthViolation (kb/Work PB1615).
display: a literal longer than 160 character positions
vcr: VCR row 7.43 (literal length bound 160 -> 8,191 at 2014); kb/Work PB1615
